LEARNING PATH LESSON · SIGHT WORDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Here — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

Five minutes, one card: you will point at your feet and say “here”, then point to a far wall and say “there”, and your child will meet “here” in a real sentence, “I am here.” By the end, “here” should be a word they know at a glance.

What is this?

“Here” is a place and direction word. On this card, a boy points firmly down at the spot where he stands, with the word printed in big, clear letters underneath.

What does it mean?

“Here” tells us where something is or which way it goes, as in “I am here.”

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs to recognise “here” at a glance, say it clearly, and begin to hear it in the stories you read together. Good hunting grounds: roll call, hide-and-seek and “come over here”.

Why this matters

Place words like “here” give a child the language of where things are, which is the first step to following directions on a page.

What it teaches

Spatial language, following simple directions and recognition of a high-frequency word.

Words to learn

wordreadplace

Say this to your child

“Look at this card. It says ‘here’. I am here. Now you say ‘here’. Well done!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and read “here” clearly, running your finger under the letters. Let your child say it back, twice.
  2. Look at the picture together: a boy points firmly down at the spot where he stands. Ask what is happening, then link the picture to the word.
  3. Play one tiny game: point at your feet and say “here”, then point to a far wall and say “there”. Read the word one last time and stop while it is still fun.

Look closer at the picture

Point to the word first, then to the picture. Cover the picture with your hand and read the word; lift your hand to check. Then let your child trace the first letter with one finger.

Ask your child

“What does the card say?” “Can you show me “here” with your body?” “Where is the boy in the picture?” — answered with a read-aloud, a movement and a point.

What your child can say or do

Expect your child to act “here” out with their body and then say it, and to point at where things are all day.

Out in the real world

Watch for “here” here: roll call, hide-and-seek and “come over here”. Every sighting is a free practice round: point, say it, move on.

Try it together

Point at your feet and say “here”, then point to a far wall and say “there”. Finish by saying “here” one more time.

Understanding check

Tomorrow, hold up the card without saying a word. If your child reads “here” straight away, the word has arrived; if not, play the game once more and try again the day after.

Parent tips

Keep it short: five minutes is plenty. Add “here” to the pile only when the cards your child already knows feel easy.

This lesson pairs with the Here flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sight Words (Class 29).
